Chapter 10. Embracing Hope and Anticipation for the Future.
Hope can feel so delicate, can’t it? It’s easy to lose sight of it in the noise of everyday life, or when disappointment weighs heavy on your heart. But if you’ve spent any time with daily prayer, you’ve probably noticed there’s a quiet kind of hope that keeps showing up—a gentle belief that, even when things are tough, the future still holds possibilities.
Think about a young couple longing for a child, but struggling with infertility. Their days were filled with both hope and heartache. Every day, they brought all those emotions—hopes, fears, even their tears—into prayer. Over time, they discovered something surprising. Hope wasn’t just about getting exactly what they wanted. It became more about trusting that God was with them, no matter how things turned out. The future, for them, shifted from waiting for a specific answer, to simply anticipating that they wouldn’t face it alone.
Now, picture an older man at the end of his life. For him, hope looked different. He prayed for peace, for courage, and for the strength to let go. In those final days, he found real comfort in the promises he’d read in Scripture, and in the certainty that his story wasn’t ending—just changing. Hope became his steady companion, a light that stayed strong, even as the days grew short.
A lot of people think hope is passive—just wishing things would get better. But when you make hope a daily practice in prayer, you start to see it’s really active. It’s a choice, every day, to trust, to anticipate, to take another step forward. It’s not about ignoring what’s real, but about believing the story isn’t over yet.
Here’s something to pay attention to: as you keep praying with hope, your outlook slowly changes. The future stops feeling so scary or closed off. Instead, it feels more open—full of possibilities, even if you can’t predict what’s ahead. That anticipation isn’t rooted in certainty, but in trust. And that’s the real power of hope—it becomes more than just a feeling. It shapes the way you live, nudging you to believe in new beginnings every single day.
So, daily prayer turns into this wellspring of hope—a place you can always come back to, no matter what tomorrow brings.
